title: Jane Frances de Chantal (1572–1641)
hookLine: a widowed mother who founded the Visitation sisters with Francis de Sales

cards: A hunting party in the French countryside. A shot goes wrong, and a nobleman is wounded by his own friend. Within days he's dead, and his young wife is a widow with small children and a grief that won't lift.

For years she runs the household, cares for a difficult father-in-law, and prays without much comfort. Then, in Dijon, during Lent, she hears a bishop from Savoy preach, and something in her recognizes him.
The widow is Jane Frances de Chantal.

teach.b: First, forgiveness. Tradition says Jane struggled a long time to forgive the man who shot her husband, and that in the end she met him, and later stood as godmother to his child.
It didn't come quickly, which is part of why the story is told. Second, a friendship.

teach.h: A BISHOP AND A WIDOW, AS FRIENDS.
teach.b: Francis de Sales became her spiritual director, and their letters show a bishop and a widow each helping the other toward God. They wrote about prayer, her children, his work, and the quiet trust they shared.
Some Catholics point to them as a picture of a holy friendship. Third, the Visitation.
Together they founded a community of women called the Visitation, named for Mary's visit to her cousin Elizabeth in Luke's Gospel.
It was meant for women the strict orders might turn away: widows, older women, women whose health couldn't take harsh fasting. At first the sisters went out to visit the sick and poor.
Church authorities then required them to live enclosed, and the community adapted, with prayer at its center. Fourth, widows.

Jane knew from the inside what the letter of James says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father, is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their tribulation."
She had been the widow in that line.
She spent the rest of her life making a home for others.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Jane Frances de Chantal, and Visitation monasteries and schools carry on the community she founded with Francis de Sales; some parishes keep ministries for widows and the bereaved in her name.

games.q: you're Jane. you've met the man who shot your husband. he has a child, and asks you to be godmother. what do you do?
o: refuse, and never see him again.
say yes, and stand as godmother.
say you'll pray about it for a year.
games.why: tradition says she agreed, after a long struggle to forgive.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has lost a husband or wife, a grandparent, a neighbor, a friend's mother, and let the empty side of their table be real for a moment: the meals for one, the decisions alone.
If you pray, ask Jane Frances de Chantal to pray for them; if not, simply hold them, and notice whether a small way to visit comes to mind.

orig.note: Greek: widow. the letter of James uses this word (in the plural) for the widows true religion visits.
